featured_reviews.name: Air Ip
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was admitted to KJ Cure Hospital for an operation, trusting that I would be in safe and professional hands. What I experienced instead was nothing short of horrifying and completely unacceptable.

To begin with, this hospital doesn’t even have a proper ICU facility. Despite this, they assured us that everything was under control and that sufficient oxygen would be arranged for the procedure. We were repeatedly told there was “nothing to worry about.”

However, mid-operation, there was an actual shortage of oxygen.

This created sheer panic among my family members and caused immense mental stress and trauma—something no patient or family should ever have to go through, especially during a critical medical procedure. This is not a small oversight; it is a life-threatening failure.

The staff is highly unprofessional and appears to be underqualified, with little to no understanding of how to handle patients or critical situations. Instead of experienced doctors, the environment feels like it is being run by inexperienced individuals who are not equipped to deal with real medical responsibilities.

This level of negligence, false assurance, and lack of basic medical infrastructure is beyond unacceptable for any hospital. It raises serious concerns about patient safety and ethical responsibility.

I strongly advise others to think twice before trusting this institution with something as important as their health or the health of their loved ones.

When my wife showed her the reports, the doctor said, “These are old reports, bring new ones.” My wife politely asked the doctor to please check the date, as they were the latest reports. After checking, the doctor had no answer and went silent.
Is this really the level of professionalism expected from doctors at such a reputed hospital?
This entire experience was extremely disappointing. A hospital of this level should focus on basic respect, patient dignity, and proper communication. The staff and doctors seriously need training in behavior and patient handling.
